s.en: Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug
s.es: busca por bisección el commit que introdujo un fallo

syn: git bisect start [--term-(bad|new)=<term-new> --term-(good|old)=<term-old>] ⏎ [--no-checkout] [--first-parent] [<bad> [<good>...]] [--] [<pathspec>...] ⏎ git bisect (bad|new|<term-new>) [<rev>] ⏎ git bisect (good|old|<term-old>) [<rev>...] ⏎ git bisect terms [--term-(good|old) | --term-(bad|new)] ⏎ git bisect skip [(<rev>|<range>)...]

good.es: Marca el commit actual como bueno.

bad.es: Marca el commit actual como malo.

reset.es: Termina y vuelve a donde estabas.
reset.en: Finish and return to where you were.

run.es: Automatiza la búsqueda con un script.
run.en: Automate the search with a script.

o.en: Do not checkout the new working tree at each iteration of the bisection process. Instead just update the reference named BISECT_HEAD to make it point to the commit that should be tested. This option may be useful when the test you would perform in each step does not require a checked out tree.

Follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit. In detecting regressions introduced through the merging of a branch, the merge commit will be identified as introduction of the bug and its ancestors will be ignored.
